report.source_text: Histopathological examination showed a low‐grade neoplasm composed of oligodendroglial‐like tumor cells with round to ovoid nuclei and scant cytoplasm immersed in a mucus‐rich extracellular matrix. Focal microcalcifications were also observed. No mitoses, microvascular proliferation or necrosis were observed (Figure 2A, Box 1). Immunohistochemical staining demonstrated Olig2 (Figure 2B), Sox10 (Figure 2C), GFAP (Figure 2D), ATRX (Figure 2E), and nestin (Figure 2F) expression.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 4-year-old boy presented with fever and convulsions. Initial imaging (CT/MRI) revealed a brain lesion with calcified foci and no enhancement. Serum neuron-specific enolase was elevated. Histopathological examination of the resected tissue showed a low-grade neoplasm characterized by oligodendroglial-like cells within a mucus-rich extracellular matrix, focal microcalcifications, and absence of mitotic activity, microvascular proliferation, or necrosis. Immunohistochemistry demonstrated expression of Olig2, Sox10, GFAP, ATRX, and nestin. Targeted next-generation sequencing identified PDGFRA p.K385L and NSD2 p.L581H mutations. These combined findings support the diagnosis of Myxoid glioneuronal tumor (CNS WHO grade 1).
